scope: Additional final-review stock-synchronization blocker associated with catalogue saves. This does not add another finding to the remaining-36 count.
finding: The local product-patch outbox stores a full cached product snapshot. Generic existing-product replay previously accepted its stockLevel, allowing a later price/name/Goods metadata save to overwrite stock reduced by a sale on another till. Generic timestamp conflict detection does not replace expected-stock CAS when the metadata edit has a newer timestamp.
fix: Native generic existing-product UPDATE excludes stockLevel. Existing stock changes are owned by dedicated stock operations; new-product INSERT still keeps opening stock. Other product metadata fields, other tables, dedicated sale and stock-receipt code paths are unchanged by this guard.

tests.name: commerce::tests::generic_existing_product_snapshot_never_updates_counted_stock
tests.evidence: Existing product stockLevel and identity are excluded; name, price, costPrice, Goods flags/order and updatedAt remain writable. Other tables retain the prior non-identity field behavior.

tests.name: commerce::tests::real_mariadb_product_snapshot_preserves_sales_stock_when_configured
tests.evidence: Real mysql_epoch_fenced_outbox_upsert inserts opening stock 7; an actual SQL sale-style decrement changes it to 6. A fresh metadata snapshot with stock 99 updates name and price to 169p but retains stock 6. The transaction rolls back and asserts zero residual product fixtures.
tests.command: POS_TEST_MYSQL_URI=<disposable socket-only test schema> cargo test --offline --locked --lib commerce::tests::real_mariadb_product_snapshot_preserves_sales_stock_when_configured -- --exact
tests.server: Fresh socket-only scratch MariaDB under /tmp/pos-catalogue-stock.fFapED; skip-networking; generated pos_stock_regression schema; no shop URI or credentials used. Cleanly shut down after companion count tests completed; daemon exited 0 and its socket was absent. Temporary datadir retained, not deleted.
tests.optionalCaseNote: This optional Rust case returns early without POS_TEST_MYSQL_URI. Only the explicitly configured actual database run reported here counts as real-MariaDB coverage.
